headline: Keep {arm:September}: at this run's unrecorded provider routing both candidates cost more per reply, and neither is shown to keep Kairo in character better.
lede: At this run's routing {arm:qwen3.8-flash} costs {contrast.qwen3.8-flash.production_replicating_cost.delta|usd_per_1k} more and {arm:1017} {contrast.1017.production_replicating_cost.delta|usd_per_1k} more; both stay within the allowed character loss, so cost alone decides. A recorded routing at which a candidate costs no more would reopen the call.

caveats.label: No provider routing is recorded for any arm
caveats.material_if: Material if a recorded routing puts either candidate at or below {arm:September}'s {cost_per_1k.September|usd_per_1k}: both sit inside the allowed loss, so the call would turn on character alone or become a trade. The earlier round found {arm:qwen3.8-flash} cheaper. Until a re-pricing says otherwise, the measured gap is the only cost evidence, and it favours {arm:September}.

Only if the uncalibrated judge marks the candidates down for replies a calibrated judge would pass, by enough to put one above {arm:September}. The cost gap is measured telemetry, not judged; its own caveat is the routing above.
Only if an aspect chosen before the results would favour a candidate; production cost, which decides, is the same whatever aspect is read.
Only if an arm other than production should be the baseline; both candidates cost more than {arm:September} whichever is called the control.

Only if a setting besides the model moved between arms and moved cost or character with it. Two did or may have: {arm:1017}'s reasoning share differed (Watch), and the simulator's request settings went unrecorded (Method). Either could shift a gap in a direction this run cannot read.

decision.text: Keep {arm:September} (the control) on Kairo. At this run's routing it costs {cost_per_1k.September|usd_per_1k}, less than either candidate, and neither candidate is shown to hold character better.
{arm:qwen3.8-flash}: costs more at this routing and holds character clearly worse, down {aspects.character adherence (v2).reading.qwen3.8-flash.change|abs|pts} points on the pass rate.

{arm:1017}: costs more at this routing and buys nothing for it; its pass-rate drop of {aspects.character adherence (v2).reading.1017.change|abs|pts} points is not told apart from zero, and on holding character alone it is worse.

The cost order contradicts the earlier finding that {arm:qwen3.8-flash} lowers production cost. No routing is recorded here, so the gap may be the provider's, not the model's; the re-pricing below settles it.

The weakest margin is {weakest.arm} on {weakest.criterion}: read on {weakest.interval}, it reaches {weakest.value|pts} against {weakest.threshold|pts}, {weakest.margin|abs|pts} points inside. On the declared {aspects.character adherence (v2).reading.qwen3.8-flash.level} reading its worst drop is {aspects.character adherence (v2).flip_margin.qwen3.8-flash|abs|pts} points. It bears on a rejected arm.

{arm:1017} spent a different share of its output reasoning ({reasoning_ratio.1017} against {reasoning_ratio.September} for {arm:September}), so its cost and character gaps may partly belong to the reasoning budget, in a direction this run cannot read.

Keep {arm:September} now. In parallel, re-price both candidates at a recorded provider routing, including the one the earlier round found cheaper: a candidate re-enters only if it costs no more than {arm:September}.

claims.text: At this run's unrecorded routing both candidates cost more per reply than {arm:September}: {arm:qwen3.8-flash} by {contrast.qwen3.8-flash.production_replicating_cost.delta|usd_per_1k} and {arm:1017} by {contrast.1017.production_replicating_cost.delta|usd_per_1k}, each interval clear of zero. The gap may belong to the routing rather than the model, which the re-pricing step settles.

evidence.caption: Paired change in production cost against {arm:September}, per 1,000 replies, at the family-corrected {family.level} level. Pairing uses only trials that report a cost, so these gaps differ from the gaps between the options table's means.

claims.text: {arm:qwen3.8-flash} holds character clearly worse than {arm:September}, down {aspects.character adherence (v2).reading.qwen3.8-flash.change|abs|pts} points; {arm:1017} is down {aspects.character adherence (v2).reading.1017.change|abs|pts}, not told apart from it. Both stay inside the allowed {aspects.character adherence (v2).margin|int}-point loss.

evidence.caption: Change in pass rate on character adherence against {arm:September}, in points, with {aspects.character adherence (v2).reading.qwen3.8-flash.level} intervals and the allowed loss marked.
The two judged persona checks, paired against {arm:September} at the family-corrected {family.level} level: both candidates are worse on holding character.

claims.text: Off-lane asks carry about half of each candidate's loss on holding character: {strata.off_lane.loss_share.qwen3.8-flash.persona.holds_character|pct} for {arm:qwen3.8-flash} and {strata.off_lane.loss_share.1017.persona.holds_character|pct} for {arm:1017}.

evidence.caption: Change in holding character against {arm:September} in the six largest slices, in points, uncorrected; read as leads. A slice's share of the loss is its drop times its cases over the arm's whole loss: off-lane asks hold {strata.off_lane.n_cases|int} of {cases|int} cases and have by far the largest drop, so they carry the shares the claim states.

claims.text: The control fails off-lane asks the same way the candidates do: {arm:September} drops character on {count.failures.character adherence (v2).September.off_lane|words} off-lane trials, against {count.failures.character adherence (v2).qwen3.8-flash.off_lane|words} and {count.failures.character adherence (v2).1017.off_lane|words} for the candidates, and on the landlord email both {arm:September} and {arm:qwen3.8-flash} brush off the ask, then answer it.

evidence.caption: Every kept off-lane failure for {arm:September}, {count.examples.character adherence (v2).September.off_lane|words} of {count.failures.character adherence (v2).September.off_lane|words}: the landlord-email and laundry cards brush off the ask and then answer it; the match-score card slips into a customer-service refusal.

The first kept off-lane failure for {arm:qwen3.8-flash}, a sample of {count.failures.character adherence (v2).qwen3.8-flash.off_lane|words}: the same landlord-email case, answered with practical advice after the turn to music.

explore.control: The allowed loss on character adherence
explore.binds: Whether each candidate counts as acceptable on character
explore.outcome: Read on the declared {aspects.character adherence (v2).reading.qwen3.8-flash.level} readings, the pick holds at every allowed loss. {arm:1017} stops counting as acceptable below {aspects.character adherence (v2).flip_margin.1017|abs|pts} points and {arm:qwen3.8-flash} below {aspects.character adherence (v2).flip_margin.qwen3.8-flash|abs|pts}; {arm:September} stays the pick throughout because both cost more at this routing.

Includes the judge's and simulator's spend; production cost is the cost a deployment pays.
Tail cost points the same way as the mean and does not change the call.

next.text: Re-price {arm:qwen3.8-flash} and {arm:1017} at a recorded provider routing, including the one the earlier round measured.
next.settles: Whether the cost order is the models' or this run's routing, and reconciles the earlier finding that {arm:qwen3.8-flash} lowers cost; only a candidate that costs no more than {arm:September} re-enters, and then character decides.

next.text: Rerun {arm:1017} with its reasoning budget matched to {arm:September}.
next.settles: How much of its cost and character gap belongs to the reasoning share rather than the model.

next.text: Tighten the existing brush-off directive so it forbids answering a non-music ask after brushing it off, and rerun the off-lane asks on all three arms.
next.settles: Whether the slice that carries most of the loss can lift for every arm, the control included.

next.text: Calibrate the judge against human ratings of holding character, starting with off-lane asks.
next.settles: Whether the candidates' character loss is real or the judge's reading of their style.

next.settles: Removes the caveats that these were set after the results and that routing went unrecorded.

method.text: {cases|int} conversations, each run {repeats|int} times per arm: {scoreboard.September.usable|int} usable trials for {arm:September}, {scoreboard.qwen3.8-flash.usable|int} for {arm:qwen3.8-flash} and {scoreboard.1017.usable|int} for {arm:1017}. Intervals are over cases, not trials.

The campaign does not state what makes a trial pass on character adherence; the pass rate is trials marked passed over trials usable. Holding character and keeping the booth offstage are separate judged checks.

Readings against the control are at {aspects.character adherence (v2).reading.qwen3.8-flash.level}. Contrasts are corrected together by Holm's method over {family.family_size|int} comparisons, each interval at {family.level}. The weakest margin is read on the corrected interval, the allowed-loss control on the declared reading.

Every judged figure comes from {judged.persona.holds_character.model}, calibration {judged.persona.holds_character.calibration}, with {judged.persona.holds_character.calibration_ratings|int} human ratings.

Production cost per 1,000 replies, at a provider routing not recorded for any arm. Some trials report no cost ({cost.unreported.September.missing|int} for {arm:September}, {cost.unreported.qwen3.8-flash.missing|int} and {cost.unreported.1017.missing|int} for the candidates). Had each candidate's missing trials cost nothing, their means would still be at least {cost.unreported.qwen3.8-flash.free|usd_per_1k} and {cost.unreported.1017.free|usd_per_1k}. Had {arm:September}'s missing trials each cost its p95 of {measure.production_replicating_cost.September.p95|usd_per_1k}, its mean would be {cost.unreported.September.at_p95|usd_per_1k}, still below both, so the order holds at this routing. The paired gaps use only trials both arms costed.

The floor on {arm:qwen3.8-flash} speaks for the pass rate; the floor on {arm:1017} reads holding character instead. Both held; the page reads the pass rate for the asked aspect and shows holding character separately.
The aspect, the control, the allowed loss and the floor were all set on {late_criteria.set_at}, after the runs.
Input tokens, output tokens and model-call counts were not reported; the simulator's request settings were not recorded on every run, so whether they varied is unknown.
